items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of joints and muscles
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesia and anti-inflammation (anti-inflammatory action) of degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis (tendon) and tenosynovitis (tendon sheath synovitis), peritendinitis (around the tendon), humeral (upper arm bone) epicondylitis (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and swelling (edema) and pain following trauma (wounds).
items.usage: After removing the release liner from the medicated surface, attach to the affected area twice a day.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, photosensitivity, aspirin asthma (asthma caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.) as a patient or a person with such experience, hypersensitivity to tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, or oxybenzone, if you are a pregnant woman of 6 months or more of pregnancy, or a child under 15 years of age.

Before using this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma, pregnant women, and breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Since photosensitivity may occur, avoid ultraviolet rays while using this medicine or for up to 2 weeks after use.

Do not use on the eyes and mucous membranes, athlete's foot, or ringworm.

When used on damaged skin and mucous membranes, or areas of eczema or rash, it may cause temporary irritation and sharp pain.

Do not use an occlusive dressing technique.
items.adverse: In rare cases, shock (hypersensitivity-like symptoms such as urticaria, dyspnea, facial swelling, etc.), asthma attack (dry rales, wheezing, dyspnea), and occasionally contact dermatitis such as redness, rash, itching, blisters, erosion, irritation, and swelling, dry skin and pigmentation, photosensitivity due to direct sunlight, and skin rash spreading to the whole body may occur; if so, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.usage: For the S-type, after removing the release liner from the medicated surface, attach to the affected area twice a day; for the R-type, cut to an appropriate length, remove the release liner from the medicated surface, and attach to the affected area twice a day.
items.precaution: Do not use this medicine if you are a person who has experienced hypersensitivity and photosensitivity, a person who has experienced asthma when using aspirin or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, a person who has experienced hypersensitivity to medicines with cross-hypersensitivity reactions to this medicine (tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, oxybenzone), a pregnant woman of 6 months or more of pregnancy, or a child under 15 years of age. Before using this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma, pregnant women, and breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist. While using this medicine or for up to 2 weeks after use, regardless of the weather, avoid outdoor activities, and when going out in daily life, cover the application area of this medicine with clothing, sunglasses, a hat, sunscreen, etc. so that it is not exposed to ultraviolet rays. Do not use on the eyes, mucous membranes, damaged skin, eczema, rash areas, athlete's foot, or ringworm. Do not use an occlusive dressing technique.
items.adverse: Shock symptoms (in rare cases, hypersensitivity-like symptoms such as urticaria, dyspnea, facial swelling, etc.), asthma attack, bubbling sounds, wheezing, dyspnea, and occasionally contact dermatitis such as redness, rash, itching, blisters, erosion, irritation, and swelling, dry skin and pigmentation, etc. may occur; if so, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Treats infected inflammatory and allergic skin conditions
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for secondarily infected allergic or inflammatory skin diseases (eczema, contact dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, atopic dermatitis, photodermatitis, chronic simple lichen, intertrigo (skin chafing), exfoliative dermatitis, itching, psoriasis (dry scale disease)), and first-degree burns.
items.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased area) 1 to 3 times a day.
items.precaution:
Do not use this medicine if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to this medicine, a person with hypersensitivity to or experience with aminoglycoside antibiotics such as streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin, neomycin, etc. or bacitracin, a patient with skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, herpes zoster (blisters), herpes simplex (blisters), chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), otitis externa (external auditory canal) with eczema accompanied by tympanic membrane perforation, an ulcer (excluding Behcet's disease), a burn or frostbite of second-degree deep type or above (not exposed), perioral dermatitis, common acne, or rosacea (strawberry nose).

Before using this medicine, patients or persons with experience of hypersensitivity to propylene glycol, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breast-feeding women, and infants and young children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Keep the prescribed dosage and administration well.

When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not use for ophthalmic (eye) use.

Do not use for purposes other than treatment such as after makeup or shaving.

Do not use an occlusive dressing technique without a doctor's supervision.

Do not use for a long period of time.
items.adverse: If contagious impetigo (crusted pus disease), folliculitis, viral infection, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, burning sensation, itching, rash, redness (congested and reddened), flushing, edema, papules, small blisters, dry skin, pustular (pus blister) dermatitis, prickly heat, wound aggravation, bedsores, pustulosis, hypersensitivity, skin discoloration, hypertrichosis (excessive hair), acneiform eruption, hypopigmentation, perioral dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, skin erosion, secondary infection, skin atrophy, striae, or increased intraocular pressure and glaucoma (blurred vision) when used on eyelid skin, etc. occur, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves bruise, stiff shoulder and rheumatic pain
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesia and anti-inflammation of bruises, stiff shoulders, and rheumatic pain.
items.usage:
After cleaning and drying the diseased area, attach 1 patch at a time, once a day.

Fix with a bandage, adhesive plaster, etc. as needed.
items.precaution:
Do not use on eczema, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc., or on wound areas.

Before using this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to medicines or cosmetics, those with an allergic constitution, and patients with severe moisture (dampness) or erosion should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Keep the prescribed dosage and administration well.

When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Use this medicine for external use only.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after using for 5 to 6 days, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If rash, redness (congested and reddened), itching, etc. occur, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Treats bacterial skin infections and secondary infections
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for impetigo, infectious eczematoid dermatitis, acne vulgaris (common acne), folliculitis, boils and furunculosis, suppurative hidradenitis, impetiginous eczema, and secondary infections caused by burns, trauma, sutured wounds, and skin graft wounds, due to staphylococci, streptococci, corynebacterium, and clostridium.
items.usage: Clean the affected area and apply an appropriate amount directly to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day, or spread it widely on sterile gauze and attach it. Limit the administration period to about 1 week. Do not apply thickly.
items.precaution: Do not use this medicine if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to this medicine, or a patient with an infection caused by non-susceptible bacteria (especially Pseudomonas aeruginosa). Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breast-feeding women, and premature infants and newborns should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Since this medicine has high permeability and absorption, do not use it for a long period of time. Do not use for ophthalmic use. Do not use on the inner face such as the eyes or eyelids.
items.adverse: If sensitized symptoms (itching, redness, swelling, papules, small blisters, etc.), temporary burning sensation, occasionally hypersensitivity reactions such as rash, mild pain and irritation, or pain when applied to patients with severe leg ulcers occur, immediately stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Treats scars and skin damage after wounds
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for wounds and scars in hypertrophic and keloid, movement-restricting, or cosmetic skin damage after surgery, amputation, burns, and accidents, traumatic contracture, and cicatricial stenosis.
items.usage: Massage lightly several times a day until it fully penetrates the wound area. In the case of a severe wound or an old scar, fix it with a dressing and leave it for one night.
items.precaution: Do not use this medicine if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to this medicine or methyl parahydroxybenzoate, a pregnant woman, or a patient with incised or unhealed wounds, or wound areas with oozing on mucous membrane skin. Before using this medicine, breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist. Be careful not to expose the wound to solar heat or light rays, and in the case of a freshly formed wound, avoid physical irritation such as extreme cold, ultraviolet rays, or strong massage. When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
items.adverse: Very rarely, local skin irritation may occur.
